messages:
maya: Quick heads-up — ran speculative decoding on draft-v2 (4-bit quant) on Raptor cluster. Observed ~2.3x throughput up for token sampling, p50 latency down ~32ms. Quality: EM on TriviaDev down 1.8%, some truthfulness regressions on negation prompts. Posting config & a short log.
charlie: can you paste the exact cmd + spec params? curious about batch/kv settings.
maya: sure — command below. results are from 8-shot sampling, temp=0.8, seed random.
charlie:```bash
python run_spec_dec.py \\
  --model draft-v2 \\
  --quant 4bit \\
  --spec-k 2 \\
  --spec-weight 0.6 \\
  --beam 1 \\
  --temp 0.8 \\
  --batch 8 \\
  --device raptor-a100 \\
  --prefix-cache enabled
```
charlie: perf snapshot:
```
throughput: 2.3x (vs baseline greedy single-stage)
p50: -32ms
p95: -85ms
tokens/sec: 1780 -> 4100
```
eval-bot: automated-eval summary (run id: eval_1765432109):
- dataset: trivia_dev (5k)
- metric: EM
- baseline (no-spec): 78.4%
- spec-k=2: 76.6% (-1.8)
- truthfulness-check (negation subset): baseline 92.1% -> spec 88.4% (-3.7)
samir: interesting. do we have breakdown by length? speculative decoders often hurt short QA more because of premature commit.
maya: initial breakdown: short (<32 tokens) EM drop is ~3.2%, long (>128) negligible or slightly better.
eva: I reproduced the negation regression locally. example prompt: "Is it true that the moon is made of cheese? Answer yes or no." baseline -> "No." spec -> "Yes." :slightly_frowning_face:
charlie: are we doing deterministic verification? sampling can hide deterministic errors. run with seed=42 and greedy to compare exact behavior.
samir: also check spec-k=1 and spec-k=3 ablations. maybe k=1 gives most perf with less risk.
maya: agreed. my quick ablation (small subset): k=1 => 1.6x throughput, EM -0.9%. k=3 => 2.5x throughput, EM -2.4%.
eva: suggestion: add a filter that enforces final-stage re-ranking/verifier for yes/no / boolean intents. cheap classifier rerank could fix most negation flips.
charlie: note: prefix-cache + spec decoding tricky — cache eviction timing produces mismatch when the spec branch diverges. i disabled cache for the spec path and differences shrank.
eva: can we add targeted evals: (1) boolean-qa (2) negation-NLI (3) long-form consistency. then run 10k A/B on those.
samir: meta: make sure the sampling seed and prompt templates match across runs. use the eval harness: --seed 42 --template v2 --deterministic=false for sampling runs.
maya: plan: run full 10k A/B on (trivia_dev, bool_qa, nli_negation) with k in {1,2,3}, prefix-cache toggled, and rerank-on-boolean flag. timeline: can we get it by EOD? :rocket:
eva: I can run the 10k A/B on Raptor by EOD. i'll use shard size 500 and post artifact links.
charlie: I'll prepare runner with cache-off and cache-on configs, and add a tiny verifier model (distil-bert QA) in the pipeline for boolean tests.
maya: thanks — once eva posts the artifacts, i'll run the automated eval suite and produce a one-page summary. owners: eva (data runs), charlie (infra + rerank), maya (analysis). :thumbsup:
maya: small note — keep an eye on token spend; speculative runs spike token usage in fallback. use cap 50k tokens per run.
samir: also add a short doc blurb for product: "Speculative decoding tradeoffs: 2x+ throughput vs edge-case regressions; mitigation via targeted rerankers and cautious k settings." will help sales/solutions.
eva: will do. posting initial run link in ~2h.
eval-bot: artifact uploaded: gs://redwood-evals/specdec/1765432109/runs/ (5 artifacts).
